properties.name: Abuja
properties.founded: 1976 (designated); seat of government from 1991
properties.summary: Planned federal capital of Nigeria, built to replace Lagos as the political centre of the federation.
properties.description: Abuja sits on the Gwagwa Plains at the geographic heart of Nigeria. Master-planned by International Planning Associates, it is organised into districts (Central Area, Maitama, Asokoro, Wuse, Garki) with the Aso Rock inselberg as a landmark. The city hosts the Presidential Villa, National Assembly, Supreme Court, and most foreign missions.
properties.economy: Public administration, construction, services, diplomacy, and a growing private-sector corridor along the airport road.
properties.climate: Guinea savanna; marked wet and dry seasons, cooler nights than the coast.
properties.landmarks: ["Aso Rock","National Mosque","National Christian Centre","Millennium Park","Zuma Rock (nearby)"]
properties.highlights: ["Federal capital since 1991","Purpose-built planned city","Seat of the Three Arms Zone"]

properties.name: Lagos
properties.founded: 16th century (Awori / Portuguese contact); British colony 1861
properties.summary: Nigeria's largest city and economic engine; former national capital and West Africa's leading commercial port.
properties.description: Lagos spans Lagos Island, the mainland (Ikeja, Agege, Mushin, Surulere), and the Lekki–Epe corridor. It concentrates finance, media, Nollywood, tech (Yaba), and the Apapa/Tin Can ports. The metro area is among the fastest-growing in the world.
properties.economy: Finance, trade, ports, entertainment, manufacturing, and the largest consumer market in West Africa.
properties.climate: Tropical monsoon; high humidity, two rainfall peaks.
properties.highlights: ["Former capital (until 1991)","Apapa container hub","Nollywood and Afrobeats centre"]

properties.name: Kano
properties.founded: c. 999 (Kano Chronicle); walled Hausa city-state
properties.summary: Historic Hausa commercial capital of the north; still Nigeria's largest city by traditional urban core after Lagos.
properties.description: Kano grew as a trans-Saharan caravan terminus. The old city (birni) retains walls, Kurmi Market, and the Emir's Palace. Modern Kano is a groundnut, leather, textiles, and wholesale trading hub linking the Sahel to southern ports.
properties.economy: Wholesale trade, leather, textiles, groundnuts, and agro-processing.
properties.climate: Sudano-Sahelian; long dry season, brief intense rains.
properties.landmarks: ["Kurmi Market","Gidan Rumfa (Emir's Palace)","ancient city walls","Dala Hill"]
properties.highlights: ["Hausa city-state heritage","Trans-Saharan trade node","Kano State capital"]

properties.name: Ibadan
properties.founded: 1820s (war camp that became a city)
properties.summary: One of Africa's largest cities by area; Yoruba political and cultural capital of the southwest after Ife.
properties.description: Ibadan rose as a 19th-century military republic, later the capital of the Western Region. It hosts the University of Ibadan (1948), Cocoa House, and a vast urban sprawl of hills and markets (Dugbe, Bodija, Oje).
properties.economy: Government, cocoa and food trade, publishing, education, and services.
properties.highlights: ["Oyo State capital","First university in Nigeria","Western Region capital historically"]

properties.name: Port Harcourt
properties.founded: 1912 (colonial port named for Lewis Harcourt)
properties.summary: Principal oil-industry city of the Niger Delta and a major seaport on the Bonny River.
properties.description: Port Harcourt was laid out as a coal and later oil export port. It anchors refineries, NLNG logistics via Bonny, and the Onne oil-and-gas free zone. Neighborhoods range from the old GRA to sprawling waterfront settlements.
properties.economy: Petroleum, shipping, fabrication, and services.
properties.climate: Equatorial; heavy rainfall and mangrove hinterland.
properties.landmarks: ["Port Harcourt Port","Isaac Boro Park","Bonny River approaches"]

properties.name: Benin City
properties.founded: Medieval Benin Kingdom (capital of the Oba)
properties.summary: Historic seat of the Benin Kingdom, famed for bronze art, earthworks, and the Oba's palace.
properties.description: Benin City was a major West African urban centre before colonial conquest in 1897. Today it is Edo State's capital, a rubber and oil-palm market, and a gateway between the southwest and the Delta.
properties.economy: Government, rubber, oil-palm, crafts, and regional trade.

properties.name: Kaduna
properties.nickname: Centre of Learning (state motto) · garrison city
properties.founded: 1913 as a colonial administrative and railway town
properties.summary: Northern industrial, military, and railway hub on the Kaduna River.
properties.description: Kaduna was the capital of the Northern Region. It developed textiles, a refinery, defence industries, and the Nigerian Defence Academy. The city straddles a religious and ethnic fault line that has shaped its recent history.
properties.economy: Manufacturing, refining (historically), defence, rail, and agriculture trade.
properties.highlights: ["Kaduna State capital","Former Northern Region capital","Industrial & military centre"]

properties.name: Enugu
properties.founded: 1909 (coal discovery; railhead)
properties.summary: Coal-mining city that became capital of Nigeria's Eastern Region and an Igbo cultural hub.
properties.description: Enugu's Udi escarpment coalfields powered colonial railways. It later hosted Eastern Region government and remains a legal, media, and education centre for the southeast.
properties.economy: Government, services, remnant mining heritage, and regional commerce.
properties.highlights: ["Enugu State capital","Eastern Region capital historically","Coal heritage"]

properties.name: Maiduguri
properties.founded: 1907 (Yerwa, replacing Kukawa as Shehu's seat)
properties.summary: Largest city of the northeast; historic Kanem-Borno gateway toward Lake Chad.
properties.description: Maiduguri (Yerwa) is the seat of the Shehu of Borno and Borno State capital. It is a livestock, gum arabic, and cross-border trading city on the Sahel fringe, with a university and a major military presence.
properties.economy: Livestock, trade with Chad/Cameroon/Niger, services.

properties.name: Jos
properties.founded: Tin-mining camp that became a city in the early 20th century
properties.summary: Cool highland city on the Jos Plateau; tin-mining heritage and tourism gateway.
properties.description: Jos sits above 1,200 m with a temperate feel unusual for Nigeria. It grew around tin and columbite, later diversification into hospitality, education, and NAFDAC-related pharma. Surrounding escarpments draw visitors.
properties.economy: Mining heritage, tourism, education, brewing, and services.
properties.climate: Highland; cooler than the plains, wet summers.

properties.name: Ilorin
properties.founded: 18th century; Fulani emirate after 1820s
properties.summary: North-central junction city mixing Yoruba, Fulani, and Hausa cultures.
properties.description: Ilorin is Kwara's capital and a historic emirate town on the road and rail between Lagos and the north. It is known for pottery, weaving, and the University of Ilorin.
properties.economy: Government, education, agriculture trade, crafts.

properties.name: Abeokuta
properties.founded: 1830 (Egba refuge among granite outcrops)
properties.summary: Egba Yoruba capital among Olumo Rock; industrial and commuter belt of Lagos.
properties.description: Abeokuta ('under the rock') was founded as a fortified Egba settlement. It is now Ogun State's capital, with cement, brewing, and a growing Lagos commuter economy along the Lagos–Ibadan axis.
properties.economy: Cement, brewing, government, and Lagos hinterland industry.

properties.name: Calabar
properties.founded: Efik city-states; major slave and palm-oil port
properties.summary: Eastern seaport and historic Efik capital on the Cross River estuary.
properties.description: Calabar was an early European contact point and later a colonial capital of the Oil Rivers / Niger Coast Protectorate. Today it is Cross River's capital, known for carnival culture, the old residency, and a deep-water port.
properties.economy: Port, tourism, government, and cross-border trade with Cameroon.

properties.name: Sokoto
properties.founded: 1809 (Usman dan Fodio's Sokoto Caliphate capital)
properties.summary: Spiritual and political centre of the Sokoto Caliphate; far-north Sahel city.
properties.description: Sokoto is the seat of the Sultan and a historic Islamic learning centre. The city sits near the Sokoto–Rima confluence and remains a livestock and grain market for the northwest.
properties.economy: Livestock, grains, leather, government, and religious pilgrimage-related services.

properties.name: Makurdi
properties.founded: 1920s railway town on the Benue River
properties.summary: Benue State capital and major crossing of the Benue River.
properties.description: Makurdi grew as a rail and river town. It is the administrative centre of Nigeria's leading yam, citrus, and soybean belt, with a university and a strategic bridge on the east–west corridor.
properties.economy: Agriculture trade, government, river and rail logistics.

properties.name: Uyo
properties.founded: Grew as a colonial administrative post; state capital from 1987
properties.summary: Akwa Ibom State capital; planned urban expansion in the oil-producing southeast.
properties.description: Uyo became capital when Akwa Ibom was created in 1987. It is known for relatively planned roads, Ibom International Stadium, and a services economy tied to oil-state revenues.
properties.economy: Government, oil-state services, construction, and trade.

properties.name: Owerri
properties.founded: Traditional Igbo town; state capital from 1976
properties.summary: Imo State capital in the Igbo heartland; hospitality and entertainment centre.
properties.description: Owerri is a compact state capital known for hotels, cuisine, and as a weekend destination from Port Harcourt and Onitsha. It sits in a densely populated agricultural belt.
properties.economy: Government, hospitality, trade, and small manufacturing.

properties.name: Awka
properties.founded: Ancient Igbo blacksmithing town
properties.summary: Anambra State capital with a long tradition of ironworking and scholarship.
properties.description: Awka is historically associated with smithing guilds. As Anambra's capital it is smaller than Onitsha or Nnewi but hosts government, Nnamdi Azikiwe University (Awka campus), and a growing urban corridor toward Enugu.
properties.economy: Government, education, crafts heritage, and services.

properties.name: Asaba
properties.founded: Igbo-Anioma town; colonial administrative post on the Niger
properties.summary: Delta State capital on the west bank of the Niger, opposite Onitsha.
properties.description: Asaba faces Onitsha across the River Niger (Niger Bridge). It is the political capital of an oil-producing state whose commercial weight also sits in Warri and Sapele. Film and hospitality have grown in the last two decades.
properties.economy: Government, hospitality, Nollywood production, and Niger-crossing trade.

properties.name: Yenagoa
properties.founded: Grew as Ijaw town; state capital from 1996
properties.summary: Bayelsa State capital in the central Niger Delta wetlands.
properties.description: Yenagoa is a relatively new state capital set among creeks and floodplains. It administers a major oil-producing state and is a gateway to riverine LGAs and coastal terminals.
properties.economy: Oil-state government, services, and river transport.

properties.name: Minna
properties.founded: Railway town on the Lagos–Kano line
properties.summary: Niger State capital on the rail and road corridor between the southwest and the north.
properties.description: Minna developed as a railway settlement. Nearby Kainji and Shiroro hydro plants give the state its 'Power State' identity. The city is a Gwari/Nupe hinterland market.
properties.economy: Government, rail, agriculture trade, hydro hinterland.

properties.name: Lokoja
properties.founded: 19th-century river port; first British colonial administrative HQ in Nigeria (1860s–1900)
properties.summary: Town at the Niger–Benue confluence; Kogi State capital and historic colonial headquarters.
properties.description: Lokoja sits where the Niger and Benue meet. It was a missionary and colonial staging post (Lord Lugard). Mount Patti overlooks the confluence. It remains a river and highway junction.
properties.economy: Government, river trade, transport, and tourism potential.
properties.highlights: ["Kogi State capital","Confluence of Nigeria's two great rivers","Early colonial capital"]

properties.name: Onitsha
properties.founded: Igbo river kingdom; 19th-century mission and trade town
properties.summary: West Africa's largest market city on the east bank of the Niger.
properties.description: Onitsha Main Market and surrounding specialist markets (electrical, building, pharmaceuticals) draw traders from across Nigeria and the Sahel. The Niger Bridge links it to Asaba. It is not the state capital but is Anambra's commercial giant.
properties.economy: Wholesale and retail trade, river port remnants, manufacturing hinterland.
properties.landmarks: ["Onitsha Main Market","Niger River waterfront","Holy Trinity Cathedral"]
properties.highlights: ["Largest market complex in West Africa","Niger trading city","Igbo commercial capital"]

properties.name: Aba
properties.founded: Ngwa Igbo town that industrialised in the 20th century
properties.summary: Southeast manufacturing and leather-shoe cluster; Abia's commercial engine.
properties.description: Aba is famous for small-scale manufacturing (shoes, garments, cosmetics, steel fabrication) and Ariaria International Market. Enyimba FC carries the city's nickname nationwide. Umuahia is the state capital; Aba is the workshop.
properties.economy: Light manufacturing, leather, textiles, and wholesale markets.

properties.name: Warri
properties.founded: Itsekiri kingdom hinterland; colonial river port
properties.summary: Delta oil metropolis and river port serving Escravos and Warri refinery.
properties.description: Warri (with Effurun and Uvwie) is a multi-ethnic oil city—Itsekiri, Urhobo, Ijaw. It hosts a refinery, Warri Port, and oil-service companies. It is commercially heavier than Asaba, the political capital.
properties.economy: Petroleum refining and services, port, and commerce.

properties.name: Zaria
properties.founded: One of the original Hausa Bakwai city-states
properties.summary: Historic emirate city and Nigeria's densest concentration of tertiary institutions.
properties.description: Zaria (Zazzau) is an ancient walled city. Ahmadu Bello University, the Nigerian College of Aviation Technology, and other schools make it a student city. Traditional dyeing (indigo pits) and agriculture remain important.
properties.economy: Education, agriculture, traditional crafts, and services.
properties.landmarks: ["Ahmadu Bello University","Zaria city walls","Emir's Palace","dye pits"]
properties.highlights: ["Hausa city-state of Zazzau","Ahmadu Bello University","Aviation college"]

properties.name: Ile-Ife
properties.founded: Sacred Yoruba city (oral tradition: origin of the world)
properties.summary: Spiritual homeland of the Yoruba; UNESCO-recognised bronze and terracotta art centre.
properties.description: Ife is the seat of the Ooni and the mythic origin city of Yoruba civilisation. The Ife heads (bronzes) are among Africa's greatest art. Obafemi Awolowo University sits on its outskirts at Ife-Ife / Ile-Ife.
properties.economy: Education, pilgrimage/tourism, cocoa hinterland, crafts.

properties.name: Nsukka
properties.founded: Igbo hill town; university from 1960
properties.summary: University town of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka—the first indigenous Nigerian university.
properties.description: Nsukka sits on hills in northern Enugu State. UNN (1960) dominates the economy and culture. The town is also known for Nsukka yellow pepper and as a literary setting (Achebe taught here).
properties.economy: Higher education, services, and hill agriculture.

properties.name: Nnewi
properties.founded: Igbo town that industrialised through auto parts and manufacturing
properties.summary: Southeast auto-parts and light-industry cluster.
properties.description: Nnewi is known for indigenous manufacturing—motorcycles, spare parts, and plastics—built by local entrepreneurs rather than colonial industry. It is one of Anambra's three urban pillars with Onitsha and Awka.
properties.economy: Auto parts, manufacturing, and trade.

properties.name: Ogbomoso
properties.founded: 17th-century Yoruba town
properties.summary: Large Yoruba city between Ibadan and Ilorin; Baptist and educational heritage.
properties.description: Ogbomoso is among the largest Yoruba cities by population after Ibadan and Lagos. It hosts LAUTECH (shared history with Oyo/Osun) and is a gateway to northern Oyo.
properties.economy: Education, trade, and agriculture hinterland.

properties.name: Bauchi
properties.founded: Early 19th-century Fulani emirate town (Yakubu)
properties.summary: Bauchi State capital at the edge of the Jos Plateau hinterland.
properties.description: Bauchi is the gateway to Yankari Game Reserve. It is a mixed Hausa–Fulani–Sayawa administrative town on the northeast road network.
properties.economy: Government, tourism gateway, agriculture.

properties.name: Gombe
properties.founded: Grew as a 20th-century market and later state capital (1996)
properties.summary: Gombe State capital on the northeast corridor between Bauchi and Maiduguri.
properties.description: Gombe is a relatively compact state capital and commercial town for the Gongola Basin, with a reputation for orderly urban growth in the 2000s–2010s.
properties.economy: Government, grain trade, and services.

properties.name: Yola
properties.founded: 1841 (Modibbo Adama); Jimeta is the twin commercial town
properties.summary: Adamawa State capital on the Benue; paired with Jimeta as a twin urban area.
properties.description: Yola is the traditional Modibbo Adama seat; Jimeta is the river-port commercial half. Together they form the main city of Adamawa, facing Cameroon's Adamawa Plateau.
properties.economy: Government, river trade, cattle, and cross-border commerce.
properties.highlights: ["Adamawa State capital","Yola–Jimeta twin city","Cameroon border hinterland"]

properties.name: Katsina
properties.founded: Hausa Bakwai city-state; Gobir / Katsina emirate
properties.summary: Far-north walled Hausa city and Katsina State capital near the Niger border.
properties.description: Katsina was a major trans-Saharan entrepôt rivalling Kano. It retains Gobarau minaret heritage and is a centre of Islamic learning. The modern city is the state capital.
properties.economy: Agriculture trade, livestock, government, border commerce.

properties.name: Osogbo
properties.nickname: State of the Living Spring capital
properties.founded: Yoruba town on the Osun River; sacred grove UNESCO site
properties.summary: Osun State capital; home of the Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove.
properties.description: Osogbo is inseparable from the goddess Osun and the annual festival. The Sacred Grove is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The city is also a batik and contemporary art centre (New Sacred Art movement).
properties.economy: Government, culture/tourism, crafts, and trade.
properties.highlights: ["UNESCO Sacred Grove","Osun State capital","Art and festival city"]

properties.name: Akure
properties.summary: Ondo State capital and gateway to the cocoa belt of the southwest.
properties.description: Akure is a Yoruba city on the southern fringe of the Nigerian cocoa belt. It hosts FUTA and serves as the administrative and educational centre of Ondo, with trade links to Benin City and Lagos.
properties.economy: Cocoa trade, government, education, and services.

properties.name: Ado-Ekiti
properties.summary: Ekiti State capital in the Yoruba highlands.
properties.description: Ado-Ekiti is the political centre of Ekiti, a state of rolling inselbergs and yam/cocoa farming. It grew as a colonial district headquarters and remains a hub for education and civil service.
properties.economy: Government, education, agriculture, and quarrying.
properties.climate: Highland tropical; cooler than the coast.

properties.name: Umuahia
properties.summary: Abia State capital and former Biafran administrative centre.
properties.description: Umuahia sits in the Igbo heartland between Aba and Okigwe. It hosts the National War Museum (Biafra heritage) and Abia State University. The city is quieter than commercial Aba but central to state administration.
properties.economy: Government, education, light industry, and trade.

properties.name: Lafia
properties.summary: Nasarawa State capital on the Abuja–Makurdi corridor.
properties.description: Lafia is a Middle Belt town that became capital when Nasarawa State was carved from Plateau in 1996. It serves farming communities and is linked to Abuja by road, with solid-mineral policy centred here.
properties.economy: Government, agriculture, and Abuja commuter trade.

properties.name: Jalingo
properties.summary: Taraba State capital at the foot of the Mambilla escarpment.
properties.description: Jalingo is the lowland administrative centre for Taraba, a highly diverse state reaching from Benue plains to Mambilla highlands. It is a market town for yam, rice, and livestock from the surrounding savanna.
properties.economy: Government, agriculture, and highland trade.

properties.name: Damaturu
properties.summary: Yobe State capital in the northeastern Sahel.
properties.description: Damaturu is a planned state capital replacing Nguru. It lies in semi-arid country important for millet, sorghum, and transhumance. Security challenges since the 2010s have affected growth.
properties.economy: Government, farming, and livestock.

properties.name: Dutse
properties.summary: Jigawa State capital; planned city of the 1990s.
properties.description: Dutse was built as a greenfield capital for Jigawa when it split from Kano. The city features wide boulevards and is known for the Dutse Rock (inselberg) and nearby irrigated rice schemes.
properties.economy: Government, rice irrigation, and Kano hinterland trade.

properties.name: Birnin Kebbi
properties.summary: Kebbi State capital on the Sokoto–Rima river system.
properties.description: Birnin Kebbi is an ancient Hausa town that became capital of Kebbi State in 1991. It is a rice and millet market near the Niger border and the Argungu fishing festival (Argungu nearby).
properties.economy: Rice, fishing festival tourism, government, and border trade.
properties.climate: Sahel fringe; seasonal flooding on Rima.

properties.name: Gusau
properties.summary: Zamfara State capital in the northwest savanna.
properties.description: Gusau is the administrative centre of Zamfara, a state known for agriculture and gold mining (informal). The city markets groundnuts, cotton, and livestock from the surrounding savanna.
properties.economy: Agriculture, informal gold, government.

properties.name: Ikeja
properties.summary: Lagos State capital and main airport city of the megacity.
properties.description: Ikeja is the official capital of Lagos State and home to Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Computer Village (Africa's largest electronics market), and Alausa secretariat. It is the administrative counterpart to commercial Lagos Island.
properties.economy: Government, aviation, electronics trade, and services.

properties.name: Ikot Ekpene
properties.summary: Historic raffia-palm products and craft market town of Akwa Ibom.
properties.description: Ikot Ekpene is famous for raffia work, cane furniture, and textiles. It sits on the road between Uyo and Aba and has long been a craft export centre for the southeast.
properties.economy: Raffia crafts, trade, and services.

properties.name: Eket
properties.nickname: Oil hub of eastern Akwa Ibom
properties.summary: Coastal oil and gas town on the Qua Iboe estuary.
properties.description: Eket hosts ExxonMobil Qua Iboe Terminal operations and is one of Akwa Ibom's oil centres. Fishing and petrochemical activity dominate the local economy alongside the state capital Uyo inland.
properties.economy: Oil and gas, fishing, and services.

properties.name: Bonny
properties.summary: Historic Ijaw kingdom and NLNG island port.
properties.description: Bonny Island hosts Nigeria LNG and has been a trading kingdom since the 15th century. The island combines deep-water gas export with a rich Ibani cultural heritage.
properties.economy: LNG, oil services, fishing, and shipping.

properties.name: Sapele
properties.summary: Delta industrial town on the Benin River system.
properties.description: Sapele grew as a colonial port for timber and rubber. It hosts a paper mill and remains a Urhobo commercial centre with strong links to Warri and the delta creeks.
properties.economy: Timber, rubber, paper, and delta logistics.

properties.name: Orlu
properties.summary: Major Igbo market town in Imo State's interior.
properties.description: Orlu is a fast-growing commercial centre on the Owerri–Mgbidi axis, known for trade, education, and as a political base in Imo. It serves a densely populated rural hinterland.
properties.economy: Trade, education, and services.
properties.landmarks: ["Orlu junction markets","Imo State University teaching hospital zone"]

properties.name: Nkpor
properties.summary: Dense trading suburb east of Onitsha on the Enugu–Onitsha road.
properties.description: Nkpor is part of the greater Onitsha metropolitan trade zone, with huge motor spare-parts and general goods markets. It illustrates the intensity of Igbo commerce along the Niger corridor.
properties.economy: Motor parts, general trade, and logistics.

properties.name: Okene
properties.summary: Commercial centre of the Ebira people in central Nigeria.
properties.description: Okene is the heart of Ebiraland, known for cloth weaving (Okene cloth), yam markets, and iron ore nearby at Itakpe. It sits on the Abuja–Lokoja highway with strong Middle Belt links.
properties.economy: Weaving, mining, agriculture, and trade.

properties.name: Mubi
properties.summary: Border trade town in northern Adamawa near Cameroon.
properties.description: Mubi is a major market linking Nigeria to Cameroon on the Mandara foothills. It trades grain, livestock, and manufactured goods across the border and serves as a northern Adamawa commercial hub.
properties.economy: Cross-border trade, agriculture, and services.

properties.name: Potiskum
properties.nickname: Largest cattle market in West Africa
properties.summary: Major Sahel market town famous for livestock trading.
properties.description: Potiskum hosts one of the largest cattle markets in West Africa, drawing pastoralists from across the Sahel. It is the commercial rival to Damaturu and a hub for grain and livestock.
properties.economy: Livestock, grain trade, and services.

properties.name: Gboko
properties.summary: Tiv commercial centre and major yam market of Benue.
properties.description: Gboko is the traditional economic capital of the Tiv people and one of Nigeria's largest yam markets. Dangote Cement plant nearby has transformed the local industrial base.
properties.economy: Yam trade, cement, and agriculture.
properties.climate: Guinea savanna; seasonal floods on tributaries.

properties.name: Ikorodu
properties.summary: Fast-growing Lagos corridor town toward Ijebu and Ogun.
properties.description: Ikorodu sits on the northeast fringe of Lagos State along the Lagos Lagoon. It has absorbed much of the megacity's sprawl, with residential estates and lagoon fishing.
properties.economy: Commuter housing, fishing, and local services.

properties.name: Badagry
properties.summary: Historic Atlantic slave-trade port west of Lagos.
properties.description: Badagry was a major slave-export port and early mission station (first storey building in Nigeria). Today it is a heritage tourism destination on the Benin Republic border with beaches and museums.
properties.economy: Heritage tourism, fishing, and border trade.
properties.landmarks: ["Point of No Return","Badagry Heritage Museum","First Storey Building"]

properties.name: Epe
properties.summary: Lagoon fishing town at the eastern end of Lekki–Epe corridor.
properties.description: Epe is known for fish markets and lagoon culture at the mouth of the Lekki Peninsula development corridor. It balances traditional fishing with rapid peri-urban growth toward the refinery zone.
properties.economy: Fishing, Lekki corridor services, and agriculture.

properties.name: Suleja
properties.summary: Historic Gwari town and Abuja commuter hub in Niger State.
properties.description: Suleja predates Abuja and was a colonial mining and market centre. Today it is a major dormitory for Abuja workers, with pottery heritage and the Zuma Rock approach to the capital.
properties.economy: Commuter services, pottery, and trade.

properties.name: Azare
properties.summary: Hausa–Fulani market town in northern Bauchi near Yobe border.
properties.description: Azare is a major grain and livestock market serving northeastern Bauchi and bordering states. It hosts Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University (Azare campus) and emirate traditions.
properties.economy: Grain trade, livestock, and education.

properties.name: Ogoja
properties.summary: Northern Cross River market town on the road to Benue.
properties.description: Ogoja is a Yala and Bekwarra trade centre linking Cross River to the Middle Belt. It serves cocoa and yam producing uplands and is a staging point toward Obudu.
properties.economy: Agriculture, trade, and transport.

properties.name: Funtua
properties.summary: Textile and grain market in southern Katsina.
properties.description: Funtua is a major cotton ginning and grain market town on the Katsina–Zaria axis. It serves the Hausa farming belt with strong links to Kaduna markets.
properties.economy: Cotton, grain, and trade.

properties.name: Daura
properties.summary: Legendary Hausa city and emirate on the Niger border.
properties.description: Daura is one of the Hausa bakwai historic cities, associated with the Bayajidda legend. The emirate remains culturally important and sits near the Niger–Nigeria border.
properties.economy: Agriculture, emirate administration, and border trade.
